newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber price dips, govt seeks 5,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber price dips, govt seeks 5,000 tonnes.

text.p: News that Thai government sought 5,000 tonnes of rubber managed to lift sentiment in the local rubber market, but not prices as overall demand remained low, trade sources said on Friday.
But prices were expected to drop further as the wintering season was ending and more supplies were expected to enter the market soon.
China has inquiries but has not placed orders so far, traders said.
"It doesn't look good. The buying from the EU (European Union) has been quite dull recently and I heard they are being very strict on quality," said a Bangkok-based trader.
"The short-term outlook seemed to remain bearish. With more supplies looming, the prices are likely to drop further," he said.
The Thai government entered the market again on Friday to seek 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade for July shipment. Prices are being offered at between 123.00-128.00 U.S. cents per kg.
"But the government has not indicated what kind of price it has in mind," said the source.
A senior agriculture ministry official said that since March 5 the government had bought 26,400 tonnes of rubber to prop up prices and to partly cover its government-to-government trade obligations.
The amount of supplies that was available in the market this week dropped 47 percent from last week to 103,612 kg but that barely supported prices.
The Thai benchmark RSS3 rubber was indicated around 117.00-119.00 cents a kg fob Bangkok against 118.00-119.00 cents a week earlier.
